figure: Figure 15.1 — FlashAttention: the same math, far less HBM traffic
issue: In the BEFORE panel, the red annotation reads "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". The colon attributes the O(L²) traffic to K/V row-block re-reads — but K/V row-block reads from HBM are O(L²) in BOTH the naive and FlashAttention implementations (each query tile still needs all K/V). The quantity that actually drops is the materialized L×L intermediate, which the AFTER panel mentions only as "no L×L intermediate at HBM" with no complexity label. Juxtaposing an "O(L²)" label on the left against no complexity label on the right invites the reader to infer that FlashAttention changes the asymptotic HBM-traffic class — precisely the "quadratic-to-linear swap" misconception that the book's own prose on PDF 247 explicitly warns against ("the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap").
evidence: Fig 15.1 BEFORE panel: "O(L²) HBM traffic: every query re-reads the K/V row-block". AFTER panel: "K/V reused per tile — no single global K/V pass; no L×L intermediate at HBM" (no big-O label). Prose on PDF 247 / printed 227: "the precise I/O complexity is more nuanced than a clean quadratic-to-linear swap, but the materialized-intermediate traffic is what drops". The caption scopes the "read once" claim but does not scope the O(L²) label.
acceptance_test: Relabel the BEFORE annotation so the O(L²) attaches to the intermediate (e.g., "O(L²) intermediate traffic: the L×L scores matrix is written to HBM and re-read"), and/or add a matching qualifier to the AFTER panel (e.g., "K/V reads still O(L²) — fewer round-trips, not sub-quadratic"). Rebuild and confirm a reader cannot infer an asymptotic-class change from the figure alone, consistent with the PDF 247 prose.
